script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Good afternoon, Greenway Community Garden, Helen speaking. How can I help?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Oh, hi. Um, I'm ringing about renting one of your plots. A friend said you might have a few free this year?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: We do, yes. A couple of people moved away over the winter, so we've got three plots available at the moment. Shall I take some details and start an application for you?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: That'd be great, thanks.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Lovely. Can I have your name first?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Sure. It's Martin, and the surname is Lindqvist.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Could you spell that for me?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Yep. L-I-N-D, then Q, V-I-S-T. People always want to put a U after the Q, but there isn't one.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: No U. Got it. And your address, Martin?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: It's 42 Harcourt Road. That's H-A-R-C-O-U-R-T.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Oh, that's just round the corner from us, isn't it? Near the old cinema?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: That's right, about five minutes' walk. That's partly why I'm interested, to be honest.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Well, that makes life easier. Now, the plots come in two sizes. A full plot is thirty square metres, and a half plot is fifteen. Do you know which you'd prefer?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Hmm. My first thought was a full one, but I work quite long hours, and thirty square metres sounds like a lot of digging. I think I'll go for the smaller one. Fifteen.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: That's what most first-timers choose, and you can always move up to a full plot the following year if you find you've got the time.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Good to know.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: And what are you mainly planning to grow? We ask because we try to put people with similar crops near each other. It helps with watering and pests.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Well, I'd been imagining rows of vegetables, potatoes, beans, that kind of thing. But realistically, with my job, it'll mostly be herbs. They're easier to look after, and I cook a lot, so I'll actually use them.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Herbs it is. We've got a couple of members who grow lavender and rosemary on the south side, so you'd be in good company. Next question: how did you hear about the garden? Was it your friend?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Partly. But what actually made me ring was the newsletter. The one the library sends out every month. There was a piece about the garden's tenth anniversary.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Oh, that's nice to hear. Most people tell us they saw the poster at the station, so it's good to know the newsletter works too.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: I did see the poster as well, now you mention it, but it was the article that got me.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Right. Now, before anyone can start on their plot, they have to come to an induction session. It's about an hour. We show you where everything is, explain the rules, the composting, that sort of thing. The next one is on Saturday the fourth of May.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: The fourth. Ah, I'm actually away that weekend. Is there another one?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: There is. We run a second one a week later, on the eleventh, also a Saturday, at ten in the morning.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: The eleventh is fine. Put me down for that.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Done. Now, let me tell you a bit about costs and the main rules, and you can decide whether you want to go ahead.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Sure.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: The standard annual fee for a half plot is forty-five pounds. But we do have a reduced rate for students, people over sixty-five, and anyone receiving benefits.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Actually, I'm doing a part-time course at the college at the moment. Does that count?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: It does, as long as you can show us your student card at the induction. That brings it down to thirty-eight pounds.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Thirty-eight. That's very reasonable.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: It covers your water, and the use of the shared tools in the shed. So you don't need to buy a spade or a fork or anything like that. The one thing we ask people to bring themselves is gloves. We used to provide them, but they kept disappearing.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Ha, fair enough. I've got some gardening gloves somewhere.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: As for the rules, they're mostly common sense. Dogs are allowed, but they must be kept on a lead. You can put up a small shed or a cold frame with permission from the committee. But there's one rule we're very strict about: no bonfires on the site, under any circumstances. We had a complaint from the neighbours a few years ago, and the council takes it very seriously.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: What do you do with all the garden waste, then?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: Everything goes in the compost bays, or there's a green waste collection every other Thursday.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Okay. And how do I actually get in? Is the gate locked?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: It is, yes. Once you've done the induction and paid, you'll get your own key. You'd normally collect it from the library, but they're closed for refurbishment until June, so for now keys are being kept at the pharmacy on the corner of Mill Street.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: The pharmacy. Okay, I know it.

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: You just give them your name, and they'll have it in an envelope for you.

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Brilliant. I think that all sounds good. What happens next?

script.speaker: Coordinator
script.text: I'll email you the application form with everything we've just discussed filled in. You check it, sign it, and bring it to the induction on the eleventh. Can I have your email address?

script.speaker: Martin
script.text: Of course. It's martin dot lindqvist at...
